$comment: Phase B eval gates, declared BEFORE the atomic re-index build (D-012 protocol). Human record: issue #85 verdict comment (2026-07-22). Consumed by `pnpm eval --gate`.
$baselineComment: Re-baselined 2026-10-24 (#139, INDEX_VERSION 4): transformers.js 4.3.1 / onnxruntime-node 1.30 reranker drift flips fixture sp-11 (101 vs 116, both maxRerank ~0.015 — cross-encoder noise on short fixture passages). Live eval on the v4 index shows no real regression (drops are post-July books absent from live labels). Rationale: reports/2026-10-24-v4-reindex-gate.md. Previous baseline: reports/2026-07-15-9725d1e-issue18-after.json. 2026-11-05 (#392): meta.goldenSetHash stamped (queries.json at f8bb617, unchanged since 2380568); no other byte changed. 2026-11-16 (#632): goldenSetHash moved by the heldOut flag (#632); no ranking change. Re-frozen from `pnpm eval --tag heldout` at db98db1 (previous baseline: reports/2026-11-16-08ca3695-604.json); every top-10 list and maxScore identical [17-book fixture]. 2026-11-16 (#359): re-frozen from `pnpm eval --tag hardkinds` at 5abdc650 on the 27-book / 98-query fixture (10 self-authored books 118-127, 28 hard-kind queries; capabilityKinds rule commit first). 131 of 210 existing top-10 lists changed (new books entering candidate sets); one existing Hit@1 break accepted: vector id-09 (cross-encoder noise, 119 at 0.00067 vs 105 at 0.00033). Previous baseline: reports/2026-11-16-db98db10-heldout.json. Rationale: reports/2026-11-16-hardkinds-rebaseline.md (every existing row whose top-10 list or Hit@1 changed, with the new book that caused it).

nonRegression.$comment: Existing kinds with markers now inside chunk text. Gate compares per-query Hit@1 vs the baseline report; every dropped query must be explained in the report regardless of gate color.

figureCaption.$comment: New kind: caption semantic search (target: figures). RU-monolingual queries (2) are inside this gate; cross-lingual caption queries are ungated diagnostics (known unweighted-RRF pathology, fixed by the 06-seam effort).

figureNegative.$comment: Active only once the figures cosine floor is calibrated (two-tier: fixture tier mandatory — 100% flagged, zero positives zeroed; live tier decides ENABLING only, never the release). `active` is the machine flag for that condition — flip it together with FIGURES_SEMANTIC_FLOOR.

filterLayer.$comment: #93 filter param (D-019), declared BEFORE implementation (D-012). The semantic filter is candidate-set restriction before exact brute-force cosine/topK — a pure subset of the unfiltered ranking, no ANN recall loss is possible — so no new gated query kind. Gate = (a) the unfiltered suite must not regress: the existing nonRegression block vs baselineReport re-run after the filter layer lands; (b) mandatory unit property tests: restricted searchLibrary/searchLibraryFts return exactly the unfiltered ranking intersected with the allow set, order preserved. Human record: issue #93 resolution comment.

backMatterTrap.$comment: #605 back-matter-trap queries, declared BEFORE the freezing run (D-012). Fixture books 128-131: an index page (128), a bibliography under a References heading (129), an ads + copyright page (130), each starting past 85% of its book, and a citation-dense body chapter mid-book (131, the negative, which must stay body). Each query's words are dense in that back matter while its relevant span is body text. Rule: in every mode, each listed query's relevant passage is in the top 10 and no front/back-matter passage ranks above it (row field nonBodyAbove === 0); a missing row or a missing relevant passage fails. nonRegression cannot see these queries until a baseline holds them, hence this block. Checked on the on tier and the hash tier (both run evaluateGate).

headingFrontMatter.$comment: #102 heading-structured front-matter rule (leadingFrontMatter), declared BEFORE the rule-on fixture run (D-012; Artem chose a dedicated block, 2026-10-23). Fixture 117 is EPUB->Markdown-shaped (keyword-dense '# Preface / What's in This Book' before '# **Chapter 1. **'); D-016's chapter detector claims 0 on it, so only the #102 rule demotes its front matter. nonRegression cannot see these queries (absent from baselineReport), hence this block. Counts are queries with Hit@1=1 out of queryIds; a missing query counts as a miss. The rule-off run is a committed comparison artifact, not a gate.

scoreDrift.$comment: #325 per-query maxScore drift (cosine modes only; keyword maxScore is bm25), |delta| <= maxScoreEpsilon vs the baseline, every baseline row must be matched. The #325 aggregate metricEpsilon (0.005) was REMOVED by #358: a rank 2->3 move shifts nDCG@10 by only 0.0022 over 59 positives and passed it. Rank changes are now caught exactly by listDiff. A deliberate model/ranking change re-baselines (baselineReport) instead of widening this.
scoreDrift.$maxScoreEpsilonComment: Cross-platform / ORT-drift allowance. Same-platform runs are bit-identical (max |delta| 0.0000 over 136 rows). Measured by #364 on the Linux nightly (ubuntu-24.04, 17-book fixture, 10 runs 2026-11-06..2026-11-15) vs the macOS baseline: max |delta| 0.0067 (outcome A) / 0.0059 (outcome B), inside 0.01, which stays. Re-measure before tuning it.

listDiff.$comment: #358, declared BEFORE the measuring run (D-012); it reuses the existing frozen baselines, which already hold every row's top-10 `retrieved` list. Every baseline row (all kinds, all modes, negatives included) must reproduce its top-topK list exactly — same keys, same order; a missing row counts as changed. Applies to all three tiers: `on` (baselineReport), `fusionOnly` (fusionOnly.baselineReport) and `hash` (hashGate.baselineReport). This makes gains ratchet too: an improvement also changes a list, so it fails until it is either re-frozen or listed in allowFile. allowFile entries are {tier, mode, id, retrieved, reason}: an entry allows exactly that new top-topK list (not 'any change') and needs a non-empty reason. Ties are broken by id (#392 decision 3), so on the hash tier a list that differs only across platforms is a nondeterminism bug to fix, never an allow entry. On the model tiers (on, fusionOnly) Linux runner CPUs drift numerically in ONNX Runtime (93-108 of 204 lists change per nightly, #364), so the Linux rule (`linux` below) reports their list diff instead of failing; macOS keeps it exact.
listDiff.$decisionsComment: #392 decisions (Artem, 2026-11-05). (1) Keep the ratchet on all three tiers, hash tier included; a deliberate hash-tier change re-freezes in one command, `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` (it also drops the now-stale hash-tier allow-file entries), and the hash-tier list-diff failure names that command. (3) Ties get a total tie-break by id; that is a ranking change, so it lands in its own PR with a full `pnpm eval --gate` and a re-freeze (parks for Artem).

linux.$comment: #364 Linux nightly rule (Artem, grilling 2026-11-16), declared + committed BEFORE the confirming nightly runs (D-012). `pnpm eval --gate` reads it only on linux (gateRuleFor in gate-guards.ts); every other platform keeps the exact rule. Two differences from the exact rule: (1) listDiff 'report': the top-10 list diff runs and prints its count but never fails (a reasonless allow entry still does); (2) per-query Hit@1 non-regression skips the platformDrift entries, by exactly {tier, mode, id}; a skipped break prints as info, and an entry whose query the baseline does not solve at Hit@1 is stale and fails. Everything else is gated as on macOS: negatives flagged, figure floors, heading front matter, maxScore epsilon, golden-set hash. Why not a frozen Linux baseline: the nightly alternates between two outcomes (A 7 of 10 runs, B 3 of 10 [17-book fixture, 2026-11-06..2026-11-15]), so any single Linux report fails on the other. Entries were drafted from the 10 nightly logs (agent-drafted, reasons below); after re-freezing the on or fusionOnly baseline, re-check them against the next nightly logs. Evidence: reports/2026-11-15-cebaace-linux-nightly*.json (outcome A) and reports/2026-11-13-f7f5306-linux-nightly*.json (outcome B), replayed by platform-replay.test.ts.

platformDrift.reason: 'overlayfs': the cross-encoder scores both top candidates near zero (macOS 105 at maxRerank 0.00033; Linux 110 at 0.00036-0.00037 vs 105 at 0.00032-0.00033), far below RERANK_FLOOR, so ORT kernel noise swaps 105 and 110.
RU 'chess openings' (cross-lingual): top-2 rerank scores 0.00068 vs 0.00064 on outcome A, a noise-level margin far below RERANK_FLOOR, so 109 overtakes 113; outcome B keeps 113 at Hit@1.
Same rows as on/hybrid xl-05: the reranker re-sorts the whole fixture, so vector and hybrid share the noise-level 109/113 swap.

'If-None-Match' with rerank off: on outcome B the e5 cosines shift by ~0.001 on Linux and the vector list puts 103 first (macOS 117, 103, 107; B 103, 117, 116, 107), so 103 (vector 1, keyword 4) ties 107 (keyword 1, vector 4) in RRF and the id tie-break picks 103. Keyword is unchanged; outcome A keeps 107 at Hit@1.

goldenSet.$comment: #392 decision 2 (Artem, 2026-11-05), declared + committed BEFORE the baselines are stamped/re-frozen (D-012). Replaces what the removed #325 aggregate ε used to catch: a queries.json relevance-label edit that leaves every top-10 list identical. Every baseline records goldenSetHash = sha256 of the canonical (parsed, re-serialized) queries.json it was measured on: queries, kinds and relevance labels; formatting does not count. A run whose hash differs from its baseline's, or a baseline with no hash, fails that tier. Fix = re-freeze the baseline (rule first): `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` for hash, a new `pnpm eval` run for on/fusionOnly. Fixture corpus edits are not hashed: span labels already fail the harness loudly when a fixture edit moves them.

fusionOnly.$comment: #356 fusion-only tier, declared + committed BEFORE the run that freezes its baseline (D-012). With rerank ON, RERANK_POOL (30) covers the whole fixture, so the cross-encoder re-sorts every candidate and a fusion regression is invisible (ON hybrid == vector on all 59 positives). This tier re-runs the suite with --rerank off and compares per-query Hit@1 against a second frozen baseline (fusionOnly.baselineReport, a --rerank off run at the rule commit): no query with Hit@1 = 1 in that baseline may break, in any mode. Cross-lingual queries are report-only (OFF hybrid gets 0/8 today; no floor until fusion is fixed) — their drops are listed but never fail the gate. A query missing from the current run counts as broken. `pnpm eval --gate` runs and prints both passes (ON = the blocks above, OFF = this block).
fusionOnly.$baselineComment: Frozen from `pnpm eval --rerank off --tag rerankoff` at b1c8ce2, the rule commit (D-012). OFF Hit@1 hybrid 46/59, vector 47/59, keyword 47/59; cross-lingual hit@1 hybrid 0/8, vector 2/8. 2026-11-05 (#392): meta.goldenSetHash stamped (queries.json at b1c8ce2, unchanged since 2380568); no other byte changed. Re-frozen 2026-11-05 from the `pnpm eval --gate --tag tiebreak` OFF pass at eec059d (#392 decision 3, total tie-break by id; no rule change): 6 hybrid top-10 lists reordered among tied RRF scores (sp-01, sp-04, spb-01, xl-08, neg-03, fig-04), spb-01 Hit@1 0→1 (OFF hybrid 46/59 → 47/59), nothing worse; vector/keyword identical. Previous baseline: reports/2026-11-04-b1c8ce2-rerankoff.json. 2026-11-16 (#632): goldenSetHash moved by the heldOut flag (#632); no ranking change. Re-frozen from `pnpm eval --rerank off --tag heldout-rerankoff` at db98db1 (previous baseline: reports/2026-11-16-44dcf56e-634-rerankoff.json); every top-10 list and maxScore identical [17-book fixture]. 2026-11-16 (#359): re-frozen from `pnpm eval --rerank off --tag hardkinds-rerankoff` at 5abdc650 on the 27-book / 98-query fixture. 131 of 210 existing top-10 lists changed; one existing Hit@1 break accepted: vector sp-01 (e5 margin 0.0004, book 122 0.8383 vs 101 0.8379). Previous baseline: reports/2026-11-16-db98db10-heldout-rerankoff.json. Rationale: reports/2026-11-16-hardkinds-rebaseline.md (every existing row whose top-10 list or Hit@1 changed, with the new book that caused it).

hashGate.$comment: #357 tier-0 model-free gate, declared + committed BEFORE the run that freezes its baseline (D-012). Runs inside `pnpm test` (vitest): the full golden set through the real pipeline with the hash embedder (hash-embedder.ts, FNV-1a bag-of-words — no model, no network), reranker off, all three modes. Compared against hashGate.baselineReport (per-query RANKS, never float scores, so it holds across macOS/Linux and Node 22/24) with the same per-query Hit@1 non-regression rule as nonRegression: no query with Hit@1 = 1 in the baseline may break, in any mode; a missing query counts as broken. The hash embedder is lexical-only, so its absolute numbers are low (no cross-lingual power) — it gates drift in chunking, FTS, stemming, fusion and front-matter demotion, not quality. A deliberate change to that pipeline re-freezes the baseline (rule first); a platform-dependent rank is a nondeterminism bug to fix, never a reason to loosen this.
hashGate.$baselineComment: Frozen by `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` at 0c9c763 (rule 44b012c + freeze tooling), macOS / Node 24. Hit@1: hybrid 37/59, vector 26/59, keyword 49/59. Re-frozen 2026-11-05 at edf91cb (#392 golden-set rule 875f7ad): adds goldenSetHash, every rank and top-10 list identical. Re-frozen 2026-11-05 at e9abff2 (#392 decision 3, total tie-break by id; no rule change): 10 hybrid top-10 lists changed among tied RRF scores (9 reordered + 1 cutoff swap: xl-05 rank 10, 103 out / 102 in, tied at the cutoff, no metric effect), 3 hybrid ranks improved 2→1 (sp-03, id-07, fmt-04), none worse; Hit@1: hybrid 40/59, vector 26/59, keyword 49/59. 2026-11-16 (#632): goldenSetHash moved by the heldOut flag (#632); no ranking change. Re-frozen by `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` at 62396165 (210 rows); every rank and top-10 list identical. 2026-11-16 (#359): re-frozen by `pnpm eval:hash-freeze` at 5abdc650 on the 27-book / 98-query fixture (294 rows); 131 of 210 existing top-10 lists changed, no existing Hit@1 change (three earlier hash breaks were fixed by rewording the new books before the freeze).
hashGate.$maxDurationMsComment: #684: raised from 30000. #359 grew the fixture to 27 books / 98 queries (294 rows), and on the `test (24)` coverage runner one full hash run now takes ~25-55 s per file (main 4bb2e420: golden-set 25.0 s, list-diff 32.3 s, hash-gate 36.3 s; hash-tier files timed out at 30000 ms in PR #683 run 44072325429 and main 566fca23 run 44072748319). A timeout, not an assertion: no rank or list changed. 120000 leaves headroom for a coverage runner.

capabilityKinds.$comment: #359 hard fixture kinds, declared + committed BEFORE any run that measures them (D-012). They measure headroom (capability), not regressions: in every tier (rerank on = nonRegression above, fusion-only, hash) a Hit@1 drop of a query of these kinds is LISTED as report-only and never fails the gate, the way fusionOnly.reportOnlyKinds treats cross-lingual. The top-10 list diff and the golden-set hash still cover their rows, so any change to them is still seen. adjacent-negative is scored like a negative (flagged = zero results or lowConfidence) but stays out of nonRegression.negativesFlagged (kind `negative` only) and out of rerankFloor.negativeSeparation; its flagged rate and the confuser-pair confuser@1 rate are report-only axes (reportOnlyAxes.adjacentNegative / confuserAt1). PROMOTION: a later rule commit removes a kind from `kinds`; from then on a solved query of that kind may not break (no re-freeze needed: the baselines already hold its rows). HEADROOM (checked once, before the freeze, from the two re-freeze reports, rerank on and off x three modes = six configurations): each kind has >= 15% failing queries in at least one configuration (adjacent-negative: unflagged); a kind that misses it gets harder queries once, before the freeze, and the PR lists every replaced query. Keyword-mode Hit@1 on no-overlap-paraphrase must be 0 in both reports (lexical-leak guard in pnpm test). Decided: one re-baseline of the existing three tiers, no separate fixture tier (Artem, grilling 2026-11-16).

$reportOnlyAxesComment: #363, declared + committed BEFORE any measuring run (D-012). Every axis below is REPORT-ONLY (`gate: false`): every `pnpm eval` run prints it and the md report lists it, no gate reads it. Each states the trend it is watched for; promoting one to a gate is a new rule commit before the run that measures it. The new per-row fields (durationMs, snippetHasMarker, top2Rerank, spanHit, lowConfidence) are additive and optional, so the frozen baselines stay valid without them. durationMs is wall-clock, recorded only by the `pnpm eval` CLI (never in `pnpm test`), and never read by the hash tier, the list diff or any baseline comparison.

snippetMarker.trend: higher is better, target 1.0: for book-scope queries, the #243 snippet window of the first passage that holds a labelled marker shows that marker

spanHit.trend: higher is better: book-scope span-hit@1/@3/@5 = share of positive book-scope queries whose labelled marker sits in a top-k passage that overlaps its span

confidence.trend: false-flag rate (lowConfidence on Hit@1 = 1 positives) down; AUC of maxRerank and of the top1-top2 rerank margin for telling Hit@1 = 1 apart from misses + negatives up (0.5 = the signal is noise). Reranked rows only.

latency.trend: lower is better; p50/p95 per-query ms per mode, same-machine comparisons only (wall-clock, noisy)

ablation.trend: `--gate` prints overall Hit@1 / nDCG@10 per mode x rerank on/off; a fusion change shows in the OFF column, a reranker change in the ON-OFF gap. Chunk-size variants are not wired yet.

confuserAt1.trend: lower is better (#359): share of confuser-pair queries whose rank 1 is one of the query's listed confusers (a near-topic book that shares vocabulary but does not answer)

adjacentNegative.trend: higher is better, target 1.0 (#359): share of adjacent-negative queries (on-domain questions the corpus cannot answer) flagged by zero results or lowConfidence

highlightInvariant.trend: violations must be 0 (no highlight on a non-query word or a NOT operand). Not measured by this harness yet: highlights come from calibre_search's FTS path, which the fixture doesn't run.

liveEval.$comment: Before/after diff on the real library is a mandatory triage artifact, NOT a gate — live-relevance.json labels are unverified and the re-index mixes markers + figures + D-016 demotion.

rrfWeightSweep.$comment: #142 weighted-RRF sweep gates, declared + committed BEFORE the sweep (D-012 protocol). Sweep: VECTOR_RRF_WEIGHT in {1.0,1.25,1.5,2.0}, KEYWORD_RRF_WEIGHT fixed 1.0, same weights at all three fusion sites (chunk/book/figure), e5-small, hybrid mode. Three measurements per weight: fixtureOn (fixture, reranker ON = shipped default), fixtureOff (fixture, --rerank off = the fused order users get when the reranker is unavailable/busy/disabled, #156; isolates fusion), liveOn (real library index copy, reranker ON, UNVERIFIED live labels). Every delta is vs the SAME measurement at weight 1.0 (the re-measured baseline, not the pre-#97 D-012 numbers). Consumed by test/eval/retrieval/rrf-sweep.ts.

ruUp.$comment: RU must go UP where fusion has headroom. fixtureOn is expected to be weight-invariant (rerank pool >= whole fixture), so it only must not drop.

enNonRegression.$comment: EN must not regress on the two keyword-favoured kinds. Fixture: per-kind hybrid nDCG@10 drop <= maxNdcg10Drop AND zero queries of these kinds losing Hit@1 vs weight 1.0. Live has no book-scope (front-matter-trap) rows; only exact-identifier is checked there, looser (7 queries, unverified labels).

zeroBroken.$comment: The existing nonRegression gate (thresholds.nonRegression vs baselineReport) must stay green on fixtureOn, hybrid rows — vector/keyword do not depend on the RRF weights.

rrfWeightSweep.selection: Among weights passing ALL gates pick the max liveOn RU-involved nDCG@10; ties -> the smaller weight (least departure from plain RRF). No passing weight != 1.0 -> '1.0 stays'. If RU gates pass only at weights that fail EN gates -> report the need for query-adaptive weighting and STOP (non-goal to build it).

rerankFloor.$comment: RERANK_FLOOR recalibration gates, declared + committed BEFORE any measurement (D-012 protocol). Known at declaration time (only the #140 headline, PR #168): with the reranker ON, ~18/38 positive library-scope e5 queries hit@1 with maxRerank < 0.3 (as low as 0.0003) and fixture negatives scored <= 0.001. Floors are scored OFFLINE from one fixture run + one live run at the shipped code (per-row maxRerank + maxScore recorded by the harness), so every candidate sees identical rankings. Consumed by test/eval/retrieval/rerank-floor.ts.
rerankFloor.flagRule: flagged(F) = maxScore < semanticFloor (0.78; library/book rows only — figures have no cosine floor) OR maxRerank < F. Mirrors confidence()/figuresConfidence() in src/semantic/retrieve.ts. Rows without maxRerank (reranker did not run) are excluded.

negativeSeparation.$comment: HARD, fixture. Every negative + figure-negative row must be flagged by the RERANK signal alone (not leaning on the cosine floor, which figures do not have) with a log-scale margin: maxRerank <= F * marginFactor.

zeroBroken.$comment: HARD. `pnpm eval --gate` (thresholds.nonRegression vs baselineReport, incl. negativesFlagged 6/6 hybrid+vector) must stay green on a confirmatory fixture run with the chosen floor in reranker.ts.

objective.$comment: falseFlagRate(F) = flagged positive rows with Hit@1 = 1 / all positive rows with Hit@1 = 1 (fixture population; every non-negative kind, all scopes). Lower is better.

rerankFloor.selection: Among candidates passing negativeSeparation pick the min fixture falseFlagRate; ties -> the larger F (more conservative). Adopt only if it lowers falseFlagRate by >= 0.15 absolute vs currentFloor AND zeroBroken passes; otherwise '0.3 stays'. Live is triage only (unverified labels): report live negatives with maxRerank >= the chosen F and the live falseFlagRate, never block on them. Also report whether ANY floor separates cleanly (min Hit@1-positive maxRerank > max negative maxRerank).

rerankLatency.$comment: #644 rerank latency A/B, declared + committed BEFORE any arm is dumped (D-012; rule decided by Artem in the grilling of 2026-11-16). A measurement on the live library through a snapshot of its index, not a fixture gate: the fixture cannot show these arms' quality effect (RERANK_POOL 30 covers the whole fixture), so `pnpm eval --gate` on an adopted arm guards against breakage only. Arms run through RetrievalOptions (rerankPool, rerankMaxTokens, adaptivePool) set by the judged dump's `--arm <name>` via BuildServerOptions.retrievalOptions; never an env var or tool param. Shape-checked by rerankLatencyArms (gate-guards.ts) on every `pnpm eval` run.

rule.$comment: Accept an arm when the median warm hybrid latency (timings.totalMs of the hybrid calls, all scopes pooled) falls by at least minLatencyDrop vs the in-session baseline row, while blind hit@3 falls by at most maxHit3DropOverallPoints percentage points overall and by at most maxHit3DropPerCategoryPoints points in every category, cross-lingual included. With 5-20 queries per category one lost query moves that category's hit@3 by 5-20 points, so the category clause means no category loses a query net; overall (110 positives) at most one query net. Latency drop = 1 - median(arm) / median(baseline), where median(baseline) is the mean of the first and last baseline rows' medians. Cold-start numbers are reported, never read by the rule. Role 'reference' rows are never adopted; 'combination' rows are measured only when every arm in onlyIf passed.
rule.latencyMetric: median warm hybrid timings.totalMs, all scopes
rule.selection: If several arms pass, adopt the one with the largest latency drop. If none passes, nothing ships: the numbers go to #644 and ADR-0011's 'stays LATER' line gets a 'measured' note.

baseline.$comment: The shipped rerank (pool 30, 512-token pairs, no adaptive cut): no options at all, so it runs the production code path. Dumped first and last in the session.

trunc256.$comment: Arm 1: pair truncation 256 tokens; same model, same pool. Risk: the answer sits in the second half of a chunk.

pool20.$comment: Arm 2a: pool 20, 512-token pairs. Risk: losing fused ranks 21-30 the rerank would lift (#604 kind; report the #604 cases separately).

adaptive.$comment: Arm 3: hybrid only; when the vector and keyword halves share their top ADAPTIVE_AGREE_TOP (3) ids in any order (books in library scope, chunks in book scope), cross-encode only the first ADAPTIVE_RERANK_POOL (10) pairs, otherwise the normal 30. Fewer than 3 keyword hits = no agreement; vector mode keeps the normal pool. Shrunk, never skipped, so maxRerank and lowConfidence still exist.

trunc256-pool20.$comment: Arm 4 (combination): only if trunc256 and pool20 both pass, measured together under the same rule.

trunc256-pool15.$comment: Arm 4 (combination): only if trunc256 and pool15 both pass. If both pool sizes pass with trunc256, the smaller pool's combination is measured first.

pool50.$comment: Arm 5, reference only, never adopted here: pool 50 (AI-Powered Search ch. 13 over-request, ~5x). ADR-0011 rejected it on latency; it shows what fused ranks 31-50 are worth. Dropped first (with the combination rows) if a row takes more than 60 min.

protocol.$comment: Followed exactly for every row; deviations are named in the report.
protocol.machine: Same machine for every row, on AC power, Calibre GUI open as usual, no index build, eval or other search running (wave rule: one exclusive machine token for the whole session). Record CPU model, Node and transformers.js versions, the main sha the rows ran on and whether it contains #618.
protocol.index: Reads go to the wave's snapshot of the live index (CALIBRE_MCP_INDEX_DIR=<wave>/index), never the production index dir.
protocol.warm: Per arm: a fresh in-process server; 3 warm-up queries outside the judged set (discarded) so both models are loaded and the candidate cache is built; then the 120 pre-registered judged queries one at a time (parallel calls share the CPU and skip the rerank with RERANKER_BUSY). The rule reads warm numbers.
protocol.cold: Per arm: 5 fresh processes, first call only, reported per stage; not read by the rule.
protocol.order: baseline first, then the candidate arms, then any combination row, then the pool50 reference, then baseline again.
protocol.driftCheck: If the two baseline rows' warm medians differ by more than 10%, the session is discarded and re-run.
protocol.judging: Hits not yet in the shared judgment store are graded blind through #361's incremental pooling (`pnpm eval:judged:dump --arm <name> --store <store>`, then the judged-blind Workflow, judges A = opus, B = sonnet as in the baseline), scored with default store matching (not --strict-text); per-category comparison with paired intervals from #361.
protocol.report: Per arm and per scope: median and p95 of each stage (embed, vector half, keyword half, rerank, Calibre round trips, total) from the per-stage debug timings; blind hit@1/3/5, MRR and total miss per category; lowConfidence rate on positives and negatives; a quality/latency chart with one point per row; the rule verdict per row.

qualityBaseline.$comment: The rule compares each arm with the in-session baseline row (same sha, same snapshot), both scored against the shared store. The 2026-11-16 blind run seeded that store and is named here so its grades are traceable. Caveat: its book-scope rows were graded with the score label visible (fixed later by #664).
qualityBaseline.judgedBy: judged-blind Workflow wf_6ac2641c-e8c, judges A = opus, B = sonnet
